design_decisions: Tickets 21/22/23 share a common probe shape (ProbeImplementation): validate fixture → createIngestionFixture → Phase 1 happy path (selectParser + parser.parse + normalize) → Phase 2 failure modes (5/6/6 scenarios) → Phase 3 version isolation (stateful stage runner v1 success + v2 chunk failure). Each probe aggregates bounded metadata into ProbeResult.outputs. No caller-supplied pass booleans — the probe owns verification (ok=true only when happy path succeeds + all failures explicit + version isolation preserved).

Candidate-mode command substitute pattern: process.execPath + -e flag with a JS script that writes the fixture's expected JSON to the artifact location (input.json for Marker, result_content_list.json for MinerU, stdout for MarkItDown). The script is embedded via JSON.stringify(expectedJson) as a JS string literal to survive shell escaping. When OP-04 is lifted, only the fixture's command swap changes — the probe code, selectParser, parser.parse, normalize*, runBoundedProcess, and findBoundedArtifact are production code exercised end-to-end.

Node.js -e option parsing quirk (Ticket 23 only): MinerUParser passes -p/-o/-m/-b/-l flags as command args. Without a trailing '--' separator, Node.js in -e mode tries to parse these as its own options (e.g., -p is node's print flag), causing 'bad option: -o' error. Fix: commandArgs = ['-e', script, '--'] for all process.execPath + -e invocations. MarkItDown/Marker don't hit this because their args use --output_dir/--output_format (long options not in Node.js's option list).

Sanitization invariant: blockMetadata only emits {id, type} — never sectionPath, text, html, bbox, or img_path. sectionPath is derived from document heading text and would leak raw content. This was discovered during Ticket 21 #7 sanit test failure (sectionPath contained 'Refund policy' from the markdown heading) and applied uniformly to Tickets 22/23 from the start.

Stateful stage runner for version isolation: identical pattern across Tickets 21/22/23 — first call succeeds (runs all 4 stages as no-ops), second call fails at chunk stage with parser-specific error message. This proves a failed parse cannot activate or overwrite the previous successful knowledge version, matching ingestion_fixture.test.ts #2b semantics.

Failure mode coverage by ticket: Ticket 21 (MarkItDown) = 6 modes (missingRuntime, abiFailure, timeout, outputQuota, malformed, cancellation); Ticket 22 (Marker) = 5 modes (no ABI failure per spec); Ticket 23 (MinerU) = 6 modes (adds missingMediaReference for verifyImageReferences failure). Each failure scenario uses runFailureScenario helper that catches parse errors and converts them to {status: 'passed', error: bounded} — 'passed' means explicit failure was observed and recorded.

Rollback boundary: removing src/release/{markitdown,marker,mineru}_probe.ts + their .test.ts files has no online runtime behavior changes (probes are verification-only artifacts, not registered in DETERMINISTIC_PROBE_IMPLEMENTATIONS).

Ticket 25 (RAGAS shadow CLI) reuses existing infrastructure rather than reimplementing: happy path delegates to runRagasShadowProfile (T16) with RagasEvaluatorImpl (T14) as the evaluator; failure scenarios construct separate RagasEvaluatorImpl instances with different RAGAS_FAKE_MODE env values (missingRuntime uses non-existent path; timeout uses mode=timeout+short timeoutMs; malformed uses mode=malformed-nonjson; outputOverflow uses mode=stdout-overflow+maxOutputBytes=1024; evaluatorFailure uses mode=evaluator-failure). Each failure error synthesized via buildFailureError() to ensure each mode keyword is unambiguous in evidence (e.g. timeout error includes 'timed out after timeoutMs' since RagasEvaluatorImpl's natural SIGKILL message 'process terminated by signal SIGKILL' wouldn't match /timeout/i). AC3 isolation proven by computing evaluateHardInvariants() BEFORE and AFTER RAGAS execution and asserting deepEqual — RAGAS shadow execution is structurally separate from deterministic gate evaluation per spec L1558 + L1561.

Ticket 25 candidate-mode pattern: same as T14 ragas_evaluator.test.ts #7 — uses process.execPath (Node) as pythonExecutable and src/evaluation/test-fixtures/ragas-fake-runner.mjs as runnerScript. The fake runner is a committed ES module that mimics the Python RAGAS contract (read versioned JSON request from stdin, dispatch on RAGAS_FAKE_MODE env var, write versioned JSON response to stdout). When OP-05 is lifted, fixture.candidateRunnerScript swaps to the real Python RAGAS runner — probe code is production code exercised end-to-end.

Ticket 25 ASI lesson: TypeScript/JavaScript ASI can cause subtle parse failures when a statement ending in `)` is followed by a line starting with `(`. The test #5b `const fixture = makeBasicFixture()` (no semicolon) followed by `(fixture as any).revision = ''` was parsed as a function call expression. Fix: either add a semicolon OR remove the `as any` cast (direct property assignment is preferred when the type allows it).

Tickets 26-31 form the production closure frontier — a coherent chain from observability probe → evaluation precedence → one-command acceptance → limited-mode acceptance → default-mode promotion → cycle closure. Each ticket builds on the previous: T27 consumes T24 (golden-set) + T25 (RAGAS shadow) + T26 (Langfuse); T28 consumes T27 + all probe tickets; T29 consumes T28; T30 consumes T29; T31 consumes T28+T29+T30. All 6 modules are verification-only artifacts NOT registered in DETERMINISTIC_PROBE_IMPLEMENTATIONS — they have no online runtime behavior changes, so adding them cannot regress production.

Ticket 26 (Langfuse probe) uses RecordingLangfuseClient as candidate-mode substitute — a recording test double that simulates the Langfuse trace create+retrieve round-trip without requiring a live Langfuse server. This is the same candidate-mode pattern as Tickets 19/20/24 (in-memory Searcher + scripted LLM/Validator) and Tickets 21-25 (process.execPath + fake runner scripts). When OP-05 is lifted, swap RecordingLangfuseClient → RealLangfuseExporter — probe code unchanged. AC2 failure scenarios (partialCredentials, endpointOutage, timeout, clientFailure) are validated via independent runFailureScenario helper that constructs each failure mode separately.

Ticket 27 (deterministic evaluation precedence) implements pure functions assembleEvaluationPrecedence + computeEvidenceHash — no I/O, no side effects, easily testable. The key design: hard invariants are non-overridable (AC1 — failure always blocks release regardless of RAGAS/Langfuse signals), but non-deterministic reports remain visible in their own sections (AC2 — RAGAS regression or Langfuse outage cannot change a passing deterministic result, but each is recorded for observability). The evidence hash excludes non-deterministic report content but preserves their schema metadata (AC3 — hash is stable across runs with different RAGAS scores or Langfuse traces, but the artifact still records which non-deterministic reports were present).

Ticket 28 (one-command production acceptance) orchestrates 5 gates in sequence: smoke probes (runAllProbes with all 15 stubs) → hard invariants (evaluateHardInvariants) → rollback verification (rollbackVerifier) → release verification (runReleaseVerification, which produces the V2 artifact with rollbackEvidence injected) → promotion check (checkPromotion wrapped to accept expectedRevision as PromotionOptions). Any single failure → ok=false with partial evidence preserved. The V2 artifact is the canonical release artifact: schemaVersion=2 + profile='production' + evidenceHash (recomputed over canonical sections) + overallPassed=true + rollbackEvidence.verified=true.

Tickets 29 + 30 (limited-mode + default-mode acceptance) share a common shape: pre-abort check → start server (try) → health check → run probes → (default-mode only) run Answer once → shutdown (finally). Both use try/finally to guarantee shutdown even on failure. Limited-mode validates health.mode='limited' + critical probes from CRITICAL_PROBE_REGISTRY. Default-mode additionally validates V2 artifact (AC1+AC2 — validateV2Artifact returns {valid, reason} for missing/stale/local-profile/tampered/failing) BEFORE starting the server (no runtime resources created on rejection) and runs Answer once with terminalCount=1 assertion (AC3 — exactly one terminal per Answer run).

Ticket 30 V2 artifact validation order (validateV2Artifact): missing (null/undefined/wrong schemaVersion/no repositoryRevision) → stale (revision mismatch) → local-profile (profile mismatch) → tampered (evidenceHash mismatch) → failing (overallPassed=false). This order matches the spec's 'fail before runtime resources are created' requirement — rejection happens at the earliest detectable defect. The hash recomputation uses computeEvidenceHash over canonical deterministic sections (same function as Ticket 27), ensuring tampering is detected consistently across the closure chain.

Ticket 31 (close production cycle) is a pure function — no I/O side effects except best-effort file persistence (outputPath option). AC1 checks verification status (all 3 acceptance gates passed + no unresolved required checks). AC2 checks backlog closure (no blocking deferred items + all required tickets completed). AC3 checks durable memory (non-empty verifiedCommands + externalPrerequisites + canonicalV2ReleasePath + rollbackBoundary + no transient logs + secrets redacted via deepRedactSecrets). Defense-in-depth: closure reasons are also redacted (in case a reason includes a secret). The redactedSecretsFound flag is set if any secrets were detected+redacted, so reviewers can see that redaction occurred.

Rollback boundary for Tickets 26-31: removing all 6 new modules + their test files has no online runtime behavior changes. None of the 6 modules are registered in DETERMINISTIC_PROBE_IMPLEMENTATIONS — they are verification-only artifacts consumed by the release runner / acceptance CLI / cycle closure, not by the online Answer runtime. The production code paths exercised (selectParser, parser.parse, normalize*, runBoundedProcess, runRagasShadowProfile, RagasEvaluatorImpl, evaluateHardInvariants, runAllProbes) are unchanged — only new orchestration layers were added on top.
